MAIN: This is the main part of this task
Everything will be very similar to the task you practiced earlier.
You will see moving dots both in the central circle and in periphery, to the left and to the right.
Your task is to report the motion direction of the dots in the central circle by adjusting the response dial.
The main difference will be that the motion will be more difficult to discern.
When you are ready, press SPACE key to start.

trainResponse: In this part, you will learn how to respond in our task.
You will see a big, unfilled circle at the screen centre. At its edge, you will see a small, filled circle.
You can think of the big circle as a clock face, and of the small circle as a dial on the clock.
As you move the mouse, the small, filled circle will rotate around the big, unfilled circle.
When you press the left mouse button, you will hear a sound indicating that your response was recorded.
Take some time to practice rotating the small circle and pressing the button.
When you feel confident that you have understood how to respond, press SPACE key to continue.
When you are ready, press SPACE key to start.
trainMotionDirection: In this part, you will learn how the stimuli in our experiment look like.
You will again see the response circle at the screen centre. Now, however, you will also see many dots around the response circle.
Initially, the dots will move randomly. At some point, the dots will start moving in a particular direction.
Your task is to report the motion direction of the moving dots.
To respond, rotate the response dial so that it points in the direction of motion and press the mouse button.
When you have responded, a green circle will appear, indicating the correct response. Please, try to be as accurate as you can.
When you feel confident that you have understood how the stimuli look like, press SPACE key to continue.
When you are ready, press SPACE key to start.
trainTaskUnspeeded: In this part, you will learn how to ignore irrelevant stimuli in our experiment.
You will, again, see moving dots in the central circle.
Your task is, again, to report the motion direction of the dots in the central circle.
Now, however, you will also see moving dots to the left and to the right of the central circle.
The peripheral dots are not important for the task. You might as well ignore them.
When you feel confident that you have learnt to focus to the central circle, press SPACE key to continue.
When you are ready, press SPACE key to start.
trainTaskSpeeded: In this part, you will learn to respond with a certain speed.
All the details are the same as before, except that you need respond sufficiently fast.
If you are too slow to respond, there will be a high-pitched sound informing you about that.
The response deadline is set so that you should have plenty of time to respond accurately.
When you feel confident that you have learnt to respond sufficiently fast, press SPACE key to continue.
When you are ready, press SPACE key to start.

STAIR: In this part, we will adjust the task difficulty.
On some trials, the motion of the dots in the central circle will be very easy to discern.
On other trials, the motion will be very difficult.
Please try to respond as accurately as you can.
It is completely normal if, on some trials, you do not see the motion at all.
On such trials, please guess the motion direction, even if you make a large error.
This session will last until we have found the level of difficulty that we are aiming for.
When you are ready, press SPACE to start.
